text:
I’m in Thailand and needed to get a Thai driver’s license. For that, I needed a medical certificate, so I went to the nearest place for me: Thiti Clinic. I’d read some negative reviews saying the staff were impolite or rude, but I reminded myself that I’m in Thailand and the official language isn’t English—so it would be unreasonable to expect literary, eloquent English from everyone. As a tourist and guest, it’s my job to make communication easier. Since I don’t speak Thai yet, I asked GPT to help me write a polite message explaining what I needed: that I’m a tourist, I need a driver’s license, and I require the medical papers—could they please help and what should I do?

At reception, a staff member named Fatima (wearing a hijab) and her colleague Kimberly were very nice. For context, I’m a pretty intense customer—I have some temper issues and I’m not always the most pleasant person—but they stayed polite and helpful. When I said I don’t speak Thai (I know about four words), they even helped me learn a few. The procedure was very fast—no more than five minutes—smooth, and Fatima was smiling. I don’t want to point fingers, but sometimes our experience depends on how we treat people. Maybe we should first ask ourselves how we’re treating others; they might just respond accordingly. My experience here was really good and even a bit fun. Thank you! I received my medical certificate after a proper check.

A little difficult to find as there isn’t much for signage...   but I would say this is both a “Fast and Efficient” small medical facility.   Not sure I would recommend for anything outside of immigration requirements or for renewal of driver license; which is what I came here for. Especially since doctor didn’t even check for anything, like you would normally receive if retrieving this document, like checking heart, lungs, etc.  actually don’t think he even looked at me, just went to desk, he signed and I left.  Again, fast and easy, indeed.

You will need two medical certifications if you are wishing to receive both car and bike license. Total for both was 400thb.

text: Most unfriendly staff ever, that fat lady in  a headscarf just made me stand outside in the sun (as they prepare for the day, they was just opening) while there was another person already inside waiting and this is not a isolated incident but rather standard. I have been here o  my last few visits juat because it is close to where I usually stay, but since the saff in so unfriendly please "vote with your dollar" and go anywhere else in Phuket, if enough people stop going the doctor might have to look for new employees, as well he should.

I would strongly caution.
I had a blood test taken due to severe exhaustion and he diagnosed a thyroid inflammation from a standard blood test, which he discussed with my husband and I within about 3 minutes in his patient waiting room. He said it's not problem, I should take a harmless hormon for one month and come back for another blood test within 4 weeks to see if my thyroid had improved. The hormon meds were (as common in Thailand) packed in a plastic bag for me, no name, no  additional info.
As I saw my ear, nose, throat specialist due to another issue a week later I happened to show him my blood test and he told me that I don't have any thyroid problem judging by my results and before diagnosing such a condition further thyroid values would have to be confirmed. This led us to go back to Thiti and inquire about the reasons for his diagnosis to which he said: did the hormone help you? If not, then just stop taking it. We asked what we should do then. He said: "Wait and see." (How can a doctor say that after administering hormones and telling you to stop taking them!!!!)

I felt extremely stupid for having trusted such a careless doctor. You don't mess with hormone medication, and make such severe diagnosis within a few minutes.

I would strongly caution against Dr. Thiti, or advise to get a second opinion if your health matter is more than a minor matter.

On a side note: don't trust his opening hours, he closer earlier than 20.30 and opens later than 8.30 in the morning. We drove there all the way from Phuket Town just to find his clinic closed and other patients were standing in front of locked doors as well.

I will never go back to him.
